newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Papua New Guinea army says no coup in Port Moresby.
newsitem.headline: Papua New Guinea army says no coup in Port Moresby.

text.p: Papua New Guinea's defence force chief of staff said on Monday there was no coup underway in Papua New Guinea after an Australian radio report that the force's commander had demanded the sacking of the government.
"This is not a coup...," chief of staff Jack Tuat told Reuters from Port Moresby.

Australian Broadcasting Corporation radio earlier reported that the force commander and police commissioner had demanded the sacking of the government over its use of mercenaries to quell a rebellion on Bougainville island.

The ABC said the Papua New Guinea Defence Force Commander Jerry Singirok and the police commissioner had visited the country's governor-general and asked him to sack the government of Prime Minister Sir Julius Chan.

But in a radio announcement, Singirok did not say he had called for the government to be sacked. "Let me assure you that we do not intend to have any coup, I can guarantee you that," Singirok said on Kalang FM radio.
Chief of staff Tuat said Singirok had told 300 to 400 troops earlier in the day to remain calm. All troops were still in barracks.
